Global infrastructure fundraising remained 39% below last year's levels during the first nine months of 2026 despite a sharp third-quarter rebound, with three megafunds accounting for almost two-thirds of the capital raised during the latest quarter.

US alternative asset manager Bow River Capital has appointed private equity investment chief Greg Hiatrides as chief executive, succeeding founder Blair Richardson after 23 years leading the business.

Aldaron, a new US private equity firm established by former executives from Palantir and Carlyle, has reportedly closed its debut fund on about $885m.

OrbiMed has raised $3bn across its latest US and European life sciences fund and sixth Asian healthcare investment vehicle, with the latter surpassing $1bn for the first time as the manager expands its exposure to the region's biotechnology industry.

US private equity firm GenNx360 Capital Partners has closed a $285m single-asset continuation fund for food services business Whitsons Culinary Group, allowing the manager to extend its ownership of a company which has tripled in size during its investment period.

Maine Public Employees Retirement System has committed $280m to a Meridiam infrastructure strategy, taking its infrastructure fund commitments this year to $580m despite its broader real assets portfolio already exceeding its target allocation.

Legal & General and renewable energy specialist NTR have secured €330m at the first close of their latest European energy transition infrastructure fund, with three initial acquisitions providing exposure to around 1.5GW of clean power generation and grid-support projects.

Midwestern US private equity manager Mason Wells has raised more than $833m for its sixth flagship buyout fund, according to newly filed US regulatory disclosures, exceeding the total capital raised for its predecessor vehicle.
